basis: The paragraph opens with the lemma 'Et praesit piscibus maris et volatilibus coeli, et bestiis, universaeque terrae, omnique'. The printing marks neither chapter nor verse, so the extent is the lemma this paragraph opens with, placed by fitting the whole commentary as one non-decreasing walk through Genesis rather than by reading this paragraph alone.
date_basis: Bede's dedicatory letter to Acca of Hexham says the work was undertaken at Acca's asking and first carried only as far as Adam's expulsion from paradise, in two books, and was afterwards extended. Acca held Hexham from 709 to 731. The four-book redaction Migne prints is conventionally placed in the early 720s and the two-book one shortly before it; the range covers both, and no source held here narrows it. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1850 printing.
text: Et praesit piscibus maris et volatilibus coeli, et bestiis, universaeque terrae, omnique reptili quod movetur in terra; quia nimirum in hoc maxime factus est homo ad imaginem Dei, in quo irrationabilibus antecellit: capax videlicet rationis conditus, per quam et creata quaeque in mundo recte gubernare, et ejus qui cuncta creavit posset agnitione perfrui. In quo honore positus, si non intellexerit ut bene agat, eisdem ipsis animantibus insensatis, quibus praelatus est, comparabitur, sicut Psalmista testatur (Psal. XLVIII, 13).
